title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: the 'geometric case' of the functional equation of L-functions. Here X is a proper smooth curve over F_p with generic point η. E is an ℓ-adic sheaf (or Galois representation E_η) that is lisse outside finitely many closed points x. L_E(t) is the Artin–Grothendieck L-function, i.e. the alternating product of det(1 - F t | H^i_c). The first displayed formula is the functional equation for the generic representation E_η, presumably taken from the previous sheet: L_{Ě_η}(p^{-1}t) · ∏_x λ_x(E) = (-t)^{-χ^♮(E_η)} δ^♮(E_η) L_{E_η}(t^{-1}). This comes from Poincaré duality on the curve, using the dual Ě and the Tate twist hidden in the substitution p^{-1}t. The quantities are as follows. χ^♮(E_η) = χ(E_η^♮) and δ^♮(E_η) = δ(E_η^♮), where E_η^♮ is presumably the middle extension j_*E_η. Here χ is the Euler–Poincaré characteristic and δ is the global constant det(-F | H^*_c)^{±1}; both are marked 'à déterminer'. λ_x(E) is the local correction factor at a bad point x. It is the L-function at x of the virtual Galois module μ_x(E_η) = α_x(E_η)^∨ - α_x(E_η)(1), where α_x(E_η) is the stalk of the middle extension at x (the inertia invariants), a representation of Gal(k(x)). Using the elementary identity det(1 - F^{-1}u) = det(-F^{-1}u) det(1 - F u^{-1}), λ_x is rewritten as (-t)^{-β_x} δ_x L_{α_x}(t^{-1}) / L_{α_x}(p^{-1}t), with β_x = χ(α_x) (degree times dimension) and δ_x = δ(α_x) (a determinant of Frobenius). Grothendieck then specialises to E pure of weight ρ and self-dual, so that Ě ≅ E(ρ) and L_Ě(t) = L_E(p^{-ρ}t). Substituting t → p^ρ t gives the boxed classical form L_{E_η}(1/(qt)) = (∏_x λ_x)(t) · δ^♮(E_η)^{-1} · (-qt)^{χ^♮(E_η)} · L_{E_η}(t), with q = p^{1+ρ}. This is the familiar s ↔ (ρ+1) - s symmetry of a Hasse–Weil L-function of a weight-ρ motive over a function field. The bad-point data are re-expressed with μ_x = α_x^∨ - α_x(ρ+1), β_x = χ(α_x), δ_x = δ(α_x). He then checks consistency of the box: applying the equation twice, or comparing with the dual equation, forces δ^♮(E_η)^{-1} q^{χ^♮} = ±δ^♮(E_η), i.e. δ^♮(E_η)^2 = q^{χ^♮(E_η)}. This is the statement that in the self-dual case the global constant is ± q^{χ/2}, a root-number sign. He marks it '??', as something to verify. The page is a bookkeeping computation in service of writing the functional equation of L-functions of (self-dual, pure) ℓ-adic sheaves on curves in the classical s ↔ w+1-s shape, with explicit local factors at the points of bad reduction.
errors: The passage from the first equation to the first braced equation is not internally consistent as written. Replacing t by t^{-1} in the first equation gives L_Ě(1/(pt)) = (∏λ_x(t^{-1}))^{-1} (-t)^{χ} δ L_E(t), not ∏λ_x · (-pt)^{χ} δ^{-1} · L(t). Grothendieck himself underbraces the factor (-pt)^{χ}δ^{-1} as doubtful.

In the box, the λ_x factor is written as (∏λ_x)(t), although after inverting t it should be evaluated at a transformed argument (or inverted). The constant also changes from δ to δ^{-1} without justification. This is precisely why he adds the '??' consistency check δ^2 = q^χ.

The relation δ^♮(E_η)^2 = q^{χ^♮(E_η)} is correct only up to sign: δ = ±q^{χ/2}, the sign being the global root number. It holds only under the self-duality assumption Ě ≅ E(ρ), not merely purity of weight ρ.

ideas.what: Functional equation of the L-function of an ℓ-adic sheaf on a curve over a finite field, with correction factors at non-lisse points, deduced from Poincaré duality for the middle extension j_*E_η.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's functional equation for L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves (cohomological interpretation and duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Bourbaki exposé 279, 1964/65; SGA 5; SGA 4½ 'Fonctions L modulo ℓ^n et modulo p')
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 279 (1964/65); SGA 5 (exposés on L-functions); SGA 4½

ideas.what: Local correction factor at a bad point as the L-function of the virtual module μ_x = α_x^∨ − α_x(ρ+1), with α_x the inertia invariants.
ideas.modern_name: Local L-factors / local terms in the functional equation (inertia invariants, middle extension stalks)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; later Deligne's local constants (Deligne, 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles des fonctions L', 1973)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA 5 / Bourbaki 279 treatment of j_*

ideas.what: Rewriting the functional equation for a self-dual sheaf pure of weight ρ in the classical shape L(1/(qt)) ~ L(t) with q = p^{1+ρ}, and the consistency condition δ^2 = q^χ (global constant = ± q^{χ/2}).
ideas.modern_name: Root number / sign of the functional equation for self-dual motives; symmetry s ↔ w+1−s
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hasse–Weil); for ℓ-adic sheaves on curves Grothendieck, Deligne, Laumon (product formula 1987)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working-out of the shape of the functional equation (with local factors at bad points and the sign condition in the self-dual case) of results Grothendieck published in Bourbaki 279 and SGA 5. Nothing goes beyond the known theory; the open points ('à déterminer', '??') were all settled in the literature (SGA 5, Deligne 1973, Laumon 1987).
transcription_corrections: 'Supposons E défini sur F_{p^ρ}[?]' should most likely read 'Supposons E de poids ρ' (self-dual of weight ρ). This fits Ě ≅ E(ρ), L_Ě(t) = L_E(p^{-ρ}t), and the later q = p^{1+ρ}; a field of definition F_{p^ρ} would not give those relations.
In the first braced line the left side is L_{Ě_η}(1/(pt)); the right-hand L-factor is probably L_{E_η}(t), consistent with the first equation, rather than L_{Ě_η}(t).
The struck-out marginal note '[-q = p^ρ-]' is replaced by 'q = p^{1+ρ}', which is the operative definition in the boxed formula.
The marginal note at top right reads 'i.e. remplaçant t par pt' and comments on the first displayed equation.
In the last brace, the denominator is L_{α_x(E_η)}(p^{-ρ}t), and μ_x(E_η) = α_x(E_η)^∨ − α_x(E_η)(ρ+1).
